مُعَرَّسٌ (S, O, K) and ↓ مُعْرَسٌ , (O, K,) [the former of which is the more common,] A place where people alight (S, O, K) during a journey, (S,) in the last part of the night, for a rest, (S, O, K,) and make their camels lie down, and take a nap, or slight sleep, (TA,) after which they depart, (S,) and continue their journey, at daybreak: (TA:) or a place where people alight in the first part of the night, after journeying all the day: or a usual place of resort where people alight at any time of the night or day. (TA.) ―
-b2- Also the former, A chamber (بَيْت) having an عَرْس [q. v.] made to it. (S, O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
